relevance_reason: The abstract reports WGS of consanguineous Pakistani families with male infertility and biallelic or hemizygous variants in candidate spermatogenic failure genes. The SPGF104 header doesn't name a gene, so this paper probably contains the causative variant for this entry, but the abstract gives no variant-level detail.

findings.statement: Khan et al. (2025) performed whole genome sequencing on 26 individuals (3 to 5 per family) from 7 large families from rural Pakistan with clinically diagnosed male infertility, 5 of which had a history of consanguinity. They identified plausible genetic causes in 5 of the 7 families (71%): a homozygous 10-kb deletion of exon 2 of M1AP, biallelic missense substitutions in SPAG6, CCDC9, and TUBA3C, and an in-frame hemizygous deletion in TKTL1.
quotes: We recruited seven large families with clinically diagnosed male infertility from rural Pakistan, including five with a history of consanguinity. We generated WGS data on 26 individuals (3-5 per family)

We identified plausible genetic causes in five of the seven families, including a homozygous 10 kb deletion of exon 2 in a well-established male infertility gene (M1AP), and biallelic missense substitutions (SPAG6, CCDC9, TUBA3C) and an in-frame hemizygous deletion (TKTL1) in genes with emerging relevance.

findings.statement: In a Pakistani family with male infertility, Khan et al. (2025) identified a homozygous 10-kb deletion that included exon 2 of the M1AP gene. They noted that this single-exon deletion would have been undetectable by whole exome sequencing.
quotes: a homozygous 10 kb deletion of exon 2 in a well-established male infertility gene (M1AP)
we identified a pathogenic single-exon deletion in M1AP that would be undetectable by WES

relevance_reason: Reports a homozygous CCDC9 variant in a man with severe asthenozoospermia from a consanguineous family, which is the defining report for this entry.

findings.statement: Sha et al. (2019) reported a man from a consanguineous family who had severe asthenozoospermia. Fewer than 1% of the spermatozoa in his ejaculate were motile, and his spermatozoa showed severely damaged morphology and ultrastructure.
quotes: Owing to less than 1% of motile spermatozoa in the ejaculated semen, severe asthenozoospermia is a serious threat to the male reproductive health.
we identified a novel homozygous variant in CCDC9 (NC_000019.9: g.47763960C>T, NM_015603.3, NP_056418.1: p. Ser109Leu) in a patient from a consanguineous family
its morphology and ultrastructure were severely damaged in the spermatozoa containing the novel variant

findings.statement: In a man with severe asthenozoospermia from a consanguineous family, Sha et al. (2019) identified a novel homozygous variant in the CCDC9 gene (g.47763960C>T, NM_015603.3), which causes a ser109-to-leu (S109L) substitution. In silico analysis predicted the variant to be highly pathogenic. CCDC9 protein levels were significantly reduced in the patient's spermatozoa. The authors suggested that CCDC9 may be a novel pathogenic gene for severe asthenozoospermia.
quotes: we identified a novel homozygous variant in CCDC9 (NC_000019.9: g.47763960C>T, NM_015603.3, NP_056418.1: p. Ser109Leu) in a patient from a consanguineous family
The variant was highly pathogenic and was predicted to be a candidate gene for asthenozoospermia through in silico analysis.
The CCDC9 protein levels were significantly low and its morphology and ultrastructure were severely damaged in the spermatozoa containing the novel variant.
